documents.title: Machine_3 Conveyor Motor — Operating Manual
documents.content: Machine_3 is a Conveyor Motor system located in Zone B - Bay 1. Normal operating ranges: Temperature 55–80°C (optimal 65–70°C), Vibration 0.08–0.25 mm/s, RPM 2200–3000 (optimal 2600), Power Consumption 700–950 W. Motor rating: 1.1 kW, 3-phase, 415V. Belt speed: 0.5–2.0 m/s variable. Belt width: 600 mm. Maximum load capacity: 500 kg/m. Drive roller diameter: 200 mm. Belt type: PVC conveyor belt, 5 ply. The conveyor uses a Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) for speed control. Startup procedure: (1) Check belt tension — deflection should be 10-15 mm under 5 kg load at center, (2) Inspect belt for damage or fraying, (3) Clear any material from belt surface, (4) Start VFD at minimum frequency (10 Hz), (5) Gradually increase to operating speed, (6) Check for belt tracking — belt should run centrally. Shutdown procedure: (1) Allow belt to clear all material, (2) Ramp down VFD to zero, (3) Wait for complete stop, (4) Isolate power, (5) Apply mechanical brake if on incline.

documents.title: Machine_3 Conveyor Motor — Maintenance Schedule
documents.content: Machine_3 Conveyor Motor Preventive Maintenance Schedule. DAILY: Inspect belt surface for cuts, tears or excessive wear. Check belt tracking — re-tension if belt drifts more than 20mm from center. Clean belt surface and remove material buildup on rollers. Check drive motor temperature after 1 hour of operation. Listen for unusual bearing noise from all rollers. Inspect belt splices for separation. WEEKLY: Lubricate drive chain with chain oil. Check belt tension and adjust if necessary. Inspect all idler rollers for smooth rotation — replace seized rollers. Clean VFD air filters. Check gearbox oil level. Verify all emergency stop ropes are functioning. MONTHLY: Replace gearbox oil if discolored or smells burnt. Full inspection of belt for wear — measure belt thickness, replace if below minimum. Check motor coupling alignment. Inspect all rollers for flat spots or bearing noise. Test VFD parameters and fault log. Check all electrical connections in motor control panel. QUARTERLY: Full gearbox oil change. Belt tracking adjustment and full tension calibration. Motor insulation resistance test. Replace VFD cooling fans if hours exceed 20000. Inspect conveyor frame for cracks or deformation. ANNUALLY: Full belt replacement if accumulated wear exceeds 30% of original thickness. Motor bearing replacement. Full VFD service. Structural inspection of all supports and frames.

documents.title: Machine_3 Conveyor Motor — Alert Explanations
documents.content: Machine_3 Conveyor Motor Alert Guide. HIGH TEMPERATURE ALERT (Warning >80°C, Critical >115°C — motor thermal protection trips): Motor overheating causes winding insulation breakdown. Causes: overloaded belt, high ambient temperature, blocked motor ventilation, frequent starts, single phasing. Actions at Warning: Reduce belt load by 20%, check motor ventilation is clear. At Critical: Motor thermal protection will trip automatically — do not reset until motor has cooled for 30 minutes minimum. Investigate overload cause before restart. HIGH VIBRATION ALERT (Warning >0.35 mm/s, Critical >0.6 mm/s): Causes include seized idler rollers, belt splice imbalance, damaged drive roller, worn motor or gearbox bearings, belt running off-center. Actions: Walk the full belt length to identify seized rollers. Check belt tracking immediately. Seized roller causes belt burnout if not corrected within 2 hours. BELT SLIP DETECTION (RPM drop with power spike): Belt slipping on drive roller due to insufficient tension or excessive load. Actions: Stop conveyor, check belt tension, remove excess load. Do not restart until tension is corrected. VFD FAULT ALERT: Common faults include overcurrent (overloaded), overvoltage (sudden stop), overtemperature (VFD fan failure), communication fault. Actions: Check VFD display for fault code. Log fault code and contact electrical maintenance. POWER CONSUMPTION HIGH (Warning >1200 W): Indicates seized roller, excessive belt tension, overloaded conveyor, or beginning of motor bearing failure.

documents.title: Machine_3 Conveyor Motor — Operator Guidelines
documents.content: Machine_3 Conveyor Motor Operator Guidelines. SAFETY RULES: Never place hands on moving belt. Always use emergency stop rope if person or object falls onto belt. Never exceed maximum load of 500 kg/m. Do not stand on conveyor belt under any circumstances. Always isolate power before clearing jams — never clear jams on running conveyor. Ensure all personnel are clear before starting conveyor. OPERATING TIPS: Start conveyor at low speed before loading. Distribute load evenly across belt width. For heavy items, use slow speed (0.5 m/s) to prevent sudden load shock. Monitor belt tracking during the first 30 minutes of each shift. If belt makes squealing noise, check for seized rollers immediately. BELT JAM PROCEDURE: Press nearest emergency stop. Isolate power at main panel. Remove jammed material carefully. Check for damage to belt. Inspect all rollers in jam area. Restart at slow speed and monitor. BELT TRACKING ADJUSTMENT: If belt drifts left — tighten left side take-up. If belt drifts right — tighten right side take-up. Make small adjustments only (half turn at a time). Run belt for 5 minutes after each adjustment before making further adjustments. SHIFT HANDOVER CHECKLIST: Record hours run, note belt condition, record any jams or belt slippage events, check gearbox oil level, note any roller bearing noise heard during shift, record maximum motor temperature.
